events.name: Flight to Japan (continued)
events.desc: Continued from Day 1 because of time zones and what-not. We finally land in Japan!

events.name: Go to Hotel
events.desc:
After all that flying we're going to need a rest. 
 Maybe grab some food if we have the energy.

events.name: Yoyogi Park
events.desc: Yoyogi Park is the fifth largest metropolitan park in the 23 wards of Tokyo, and is divided across the road into two areas: Area A as a forest park, and Area B with an athletic field, outdoor stage, etc. in contrast to this.

events.name: Meiji Jingu Shrine
events.desc: Meiji Jingu is one of the Shinto shrines in Japan, with vast lands of forestry, located in the middle of the megacity, Tokyo. Upon stepping into this precinct, you will forget that you are in the hustle and bustle of the city, and will find Japanese traditional scenes amidst nature.

events.name: Tokyo Mystery Circus
events.desc: Tokyo Mystery Circus - or TMC for short - is packed with fun games and events that you can participate in! They offer several different types of games such as Real Escape Game, Real Stealth Game, and a projection map table game! They also have a goods shop where you can purchase TMC original merchandise, and a cafe which offers a limited edition menu depending on what games are currently hosted.

events.name: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
events.desc: Shinjuku Gyoen was constructed on the site of a private mansion belonging to Lord Naito, a “daimyo” (feudal lord) of the Edo era. Completed in 1906 as an imperial garden, it was re-designated as a national garden after the Second World War and opened to the public.

events.name: I'm Donut?
events.desc: Do you ever ask yourself, Am I a donut? “Raw donuts” were born from the desire to make people feel excited and surprised. The dough is made by kneading several types of wheat and whole roasted pumpkin, and then fermenting it at a low temperature for a long time, then frying it at high temperature all at once. I'm Donut? discovered a new texture that is chewy yet fluffy and melts in your mouth.

events.name: Mipig Café
events.desc: “Micro pig's house” is where all micro pigs from baby ones to adult ones live together, and you are a friend of them. You may want to take a nap, read books, eat some snacks etc. with your friends! Please make yourself at home and have a wonderful time!

events.name: Tokyo Plaza Omotesando Harajuku
events.desc: A neat multi-level mall area with lots of shops, restaurants, and a beautiful outdoor seating area. It's got a cool mirrored entrance that makes a great place for a distinct photo!

events.name: Kabukicho
events.desc: Kabukicho is a famous entertainment district best known for adult-oriented nightlife. Small clubs, smoky pubs, and late-night snack bars are crammed into lantern-lit alleys in Golden Gai. Robot Restaurant hosts kitschy sci-fi dinner shows, while rock bands play at Marz and Ashibe Hall.

events.name: Omoide Yokocho
events.desc: Omoide Yokocho, located at the west exit of Shinjuku Station in Tokyo, is a good old drinking district where nostalgic scenes remain. Its roots go back to an open-air market that was established on the burnt-out ruins immediately after the war. Today, a total of about 80 stores, including about 60 restaurants, mainly motsuyaki and yakitori shops, and ticket shops, are packed into the roughly 2,000 square meter area, supporting the bustle of the town and making it a popular spot for foreign tourists as well.

events.name: GiGo 1 (and Other Arcades)
events.desc: GiGO Akihabara 1 is a large arcade located in the Akihabara district of Tokyo, known for its vibrant gaming atmosphere and diverse selection of games. It features a mix of classic arcade games, modern video games, and virtual reality experiences, along with prize and claw machines.

events.name: Kanda Shrine
events.desc: Kanda Shrine is a Shinto shrine located in Chiyoda, Tokyo. The shrine dates back 1,270 years, but the current structure was rebuilt several times due to fire and earthquakes. It is situated in one of the most expensive estate areas of Tokyo.

events.name: Ueno Zoological Park
events.desc: The Ueno Zoo is a 14,300 square meter zoo, managed by the Tokyo Metropolitan Government, and located in Taitō, Tokyo. It is Japan's oldest zoo, opened on March 20, 1882. It is served by Ueno Station, Keisei Ueno Station, and Nezu Station, with convenient access from several public transportation networks.

events.name: Ueno Park
events.desc: Ueno Onshi Park, which celebrated its 150th anniversary in 2023, is a metropolitan park representing urban parks in Japan. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government has been promoting a revitalization and improvement plan based on the Ueno Onshi Park Grand Design. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government will continue to promote the development of Ueno Park to make it more attractive as a center of culture and tourism that serves as the face of Tokyo.

events.name: Origami Museum
events.desc: An intimate space dedicated to the art of traditional and contemporary origami, showcasing intricate paper-folded works, historical displays, hands-on workshops, and rotating exhibitions. It gives visitors a deeper appreciation for Japanese craftsmanship and creativity through the delicate medium of paper.

events.name: Tokyo Skytree
events.desc: Soaring 634 meters above Tokyo, this broadcasting and observation tower is the tallest structure in Japan and the second tallest in the world. It boasts two sky decks (at 350 meters and 450 meters) with panoramic city views—including Mt. Fuji on clear days—plus a glass-floored walkway, shopping at Solamachi, an aquarium, and a planetarium at its base.

events.name: Kirby Café Store
events.desc: Next door to the Kirby Café, this retail shop focuses on Kirby-themed merchandise and takeaway items, including exclusive souvenirs like plushies, keychains, mugs, and seasonal drinks.

events.name: Kirby Café
events.desc: This charming character café brings Nintendo’s Kirby to life with themed dishes, desserts, decor, and jazz-style game soundtracks—everything is shaped like Kirby characters or inspired by game elements. The combination of playful ambiance and tasty menu items ensures a delightful experience for fans.

events.name: TAITO Station
events.desc: TAITO Station is a well-known Japanese chain of arcade gaming centers, particularly famous for its wide variety of arcade games, prize games, and photo sticker booths. It's a popular destination for both locals and tourists seeking a fun and immersive gaming experience.

events.name: Hirose Entertainment Yard
events.desc: Hirose Entertainment Yard, also known as HEY, is a multi-story arcade located in Akihabara, Tokyo, renowned for its extensive collection of both classic and modern arcade games. It's a popular destination for gamers and tourists alike, offering a vibrant atmosphere with a wide array of games, including fighting games, shooting games, and crane games.

events.name: Super Potato
events.desc: Super Potato is a well-known chain of retro video game stores in Japan, famous for its extensive collection of classic and vintage games, consoles, and merchandise. The Akihabara location is a popular destination for retro gaming enthusiasts, with multiple floors dedicated to browsing and playing classic arcade and console games. It's known for its nostalgic atmosphere, with old TVs displaying classic games and vintage sweets available for purchase.

events.name: Café Asan
events.desc: Café Asan, located in the Ueno/Asakusa area of Tokyo, is a unique café known for its relaxed, hideaway atmosphere and signature soufflé pancakes. It offers free Wi-Fi, power outlets, and even iPad rentals, making it a popular spot for remote work or a casual hangout.

events.name: Owl Café Akiba Fukurou
events.desc: Akiba Fukurou is a popular owl café in Tokyo's Akihabara district, known for its unique and intimate interaction with owls. It's a café that focuses on creating a peaceful environment where visitors can connect with owls in a respectful way. The café prioritizes the well-being of the owls, with a focus on their health and comfort.

events.name: Tokyo National Museum
events.desc: The Tokyo National Museum (Japan's first and largest) houses an extensive collection of Japanese art and artifacts, spanning centuries of history and various artistic disciplines. It's located in Ueno Park and features multiple buildings, each dedicated to different aspects of Japanese and Asian art and archaeology.

events.name: 2K540 Aki-Oka Artisan
events.desc: 2K540 Aki-Oka Artisan is a unique shopping street in Tokyo located under the JR railway tracks between Akihabara and Okachimachi Stations. It's known for its collection of over 50 artisan shops, workshops, and cafés, offering a diverse range of handcrafted goods.

events.name: Copic Ciao Marker Collectathon
events.desc: Tools Ochanomizu is a specialized art supply store in Tokyo, known for its high-quality materials and selection, particularly for graphic arts professionals and students. It's a haven for artists, designers, and anyone interested in art and design supplies, including manga and architecture materials.

events.name: Mandarake Complex
events.desc: Mandarake Complex is an eight-story building in Akihabara, Tokyo, dedicated to anime, manga, and pop culture merchandise, particularly second-hand items. It's a massive, multi-faceted store where each floor is categorized by product type, making it easy for visitors to navigate and find what they're looking for. The complex is known for its extensive collection of manga, anime figures, trading cards, retro games, and other collectibles, including rare and vintage items.

events.name: Animate Akihabara
events.desc: Animate Akihabara is a multi-story store in Tokyo's Akihabara district that specializes in anime, manga, and game merchandise. It's a popular destination for anime fans, offering a wide range of products, including manga, figures, posters, stationery, and more. The store is known for its lively atmosphere, knowledgeable staff, and frequent events like autograph sessions and promotional events. It's a must-visit location for anyone interested in Japanese pop culture.

events.name: Travel to Kanazawa
events.desc:
• Tsukiji Station 
 • Hibiya Line to Ueno Station 
 • Shinkansen Hakutaka from Ueno Station to Kanazawa Station 
 • Bus from Kanazawa Station to Moriyama Ichichome Bus Stop 
 • Walk to Machiya Townhouse

events.name: Relax at Machiya Townhouse
events.desc: Nothing major planned today!

events.name: Myōryū-ji (Ninja Temple)
events.desc: Myōryū-ji, commonly known as Ninja Temple (Ninjadera), is a Buddhist temple in Kanazawa, renowned for its deceptivly defensive architecture rather than any connection to ninja. It was built during the Edo period as a secret place of worship and retreat for the Maeda clan, who ruled the Kaga Domain. The temple's numerous hidden rooms, secret passages, and trapdoors were designed to mislead and protect against potential attacks, mimicking the tactics of ninja.

events.name: Kenroku-en
events.desc: Kenroku-en Garden, located in Kanazawa, Ishikawa, is renowned as one of Japan's “Three Great Gardens” and is celebrated for its meticulously designed landscape and seasonal beauty. Spanning nearly 25 acres, it's a strolling-style garden featuring a large pond (Kasumigaike), numerous tea houses, and one of Japan's oldest fountains. Kenroku-en's name, meaning “garden of six sublime features,” reflects the six attributes of a perfect garden: spaciousness, seclusion, artifice, antiquity, water sources, and magnificent views.

events.name: Kanazawa Castle Park
events.desc: Kanazawa Castle Park, located adjacent to the renowned Kenroku-en Garden, is a large, partially restored Japanese castle and its surrounding parkland in Kanazawa. It served as the headquarters of the Maeda clan for centuries and has been extensively rebuilt and renovated in recent years. The park offers a tranquil oasis with beautiful gardens, walking paths, and ponds, providing a scenic escape within the city.

events.name: Oyama Shrine
events.desc: Oyama Shrine, located in Kanazawa, Ishikawa, is a Shinto shrine dedicated to Maeda Toshiie, the first lord of the Kaga domain, and his wife. It's known for its distinctive main gate, a blend of Japanese, Chinese, and European architectural styles, designed by a Dutch architect. The shrine also features a beautiful strolling garden with ponds and bridges shaped like musical instruments.

events.name: Nomura-ke Samurai Residence
events.desc: The Nomura-ke Samurai Residence in Kanazawa is a beautifully restored Edo-period samurai house, offering a glimpse into the life of a high-ranking samurai family. It features a stunning Japanese garden, a tea room, and displays of artifacts and personal belongings of the Nomura family, including samurai armor and swords. The residence is located in the Nagamachi Samurai District, and its garden has been recognized for its beauty, even being ranked among the top gardens in Japan.

events.name: Kaga-Yuzen Kimono Center
events.desc: The Kaga-Yuzen Kimono Center in Kanazawa is a museum dedicated to the art of Kaga-Yuzen dyeing, a traditional silk dyeing technique known for its intricate designs and vibrant colors. Visitors can explore the history and techniques of Kaga-Yuzen, view examples of the beautiful kimono and other dyed items, and even participate in hands-on workshops. The center aims to familiarize more people with this unique art form and its cultural significance.

events.name: Kazuemachi Chaya District
events.desc: Kazuemachi Chaya District is one of Kanazawa's three traditional teahouse districts, known for its well-preserved Edo-period architecture and tranquil atmosphere along the Asano River. It's characterized by narrow streets, lattice-style windows (senbonkoshi), and historic wooden buildings that once housed geishas and their patrons. While smaller and less crowded than Higashi Chaya, it offers a charming and authentic experience, particularly in the evening when lanterns illuminate the area.

events.name: Higashi Chaya District
events.desc: The Higashi Chaya District in Kanazawa is a well-preserved geisha district, famous for its historical teahouses and traditional architecture. It's one of three such districts in Kanazawa, but Higashi is the largest and most popular, offering a glimpse into the Edo period's entertainment culture. Today, the district features beautifully preserved wooden buildings, now housing cafés, restaurants, shops, and even museums like the Shima Teahouse, which has been converted into a museum.

events.name: Kanazawa Yasue Gold Leaf Museum
events.desc: The Kanazawa Yasue Gold Leaf Museum is dedicated to preserving and showcasing the art and craft of gold leaf production and its application in various art forms. Located in Kanazawa, the museum features exhibits on the history of gold leaf, the traditional production process, and examples of gold leaf art from different periods. It also houses a collection of tools used in gold leaf making and offers insights into the cultural significance of this unique craft.

events.name: Café Tamon
events.desc: Café Tamon is a popular café located in the Higashi Chaya District of Kanazawa, known for its delicious rice flour pancakes and commitment to using local, sustainable ingredients. It's situated near Utatsu Shrine and offers a relaxed atmosphere, serving breakfast, lunch, and brunch.

events.name: D.T. Suzuki Museum
events.desc: The D.T. Suzuki Museum opened in Kanazawa, Ishikawa Prefecture, Japan in 2011. Dedicated to the life, writings, and ideas of Kanazawa-born Buddhist philosopher D. T. Suzuki, the facility, designed by Yoshio Taniguchi, includes a contemplative space overlooking the Water Mirror Garden.

events.name: Geisha House Shima
events.desc: Geisha House Shima, located in Kanazawa's Higashi Chaya District, is a well-preserved, historic teahouse (chaya) that has been converted into a museum, offering a glimpse into the world of geishas. It's known for its authentic Edo-period interiors, including tatami mats, sliding doors, and elegant wooden finishes, showcasing the traditional setting where geishas entertained guests. Visitors can explore the various rooms, see geisha instruments and accessories like shamisen and kimonos, and even discover hidden spaces used for private performances.

events.name: Omicho Market
events.desc: Omicho Market, known as “Kanazawa's Kitchen”, is a bustling, covered marketplace with over 170 shops and restaurants. It's a vibrant hub where locals and tourists alike explore fresh seafood, seasonal produce, local specialties, and more. The market offers a wide array of goods, from seafood and produce to flowers, clothing, and kitchenware. It's particularly known for its fresh seafood from the Sea of Japan, including crab, yellowtail, and shrimp.

events.name: Kanazawa 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art
events.desc: The 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art, Kanazawa, is a globally recognized art museum known for its innovative architecture and focus on community engagement. Designed by SANAA (Kazuyo Sejima + Ryue Nishizawa), the circular building features a free-access public zone and ticketed exhibition spaces, fostering a unique blend of open and enclosed spaces. The museum's collection includes both permanent and temporary exhibitions, with a strong emphasis on international artists and interactive installations.

events.name: Travel to Takayama
events.desc:
• Bus, Meikan Line, to Morimoto Station 
 • IR Ishikawa Rail Line to Toyama Station 
 • Hida Limited Express Train from Toyama Station to Takayama Station 
 • Walk to Machiya Inn

events.name: Takayama Showakan Museum
events.desc: The retro streets of 1950 are reconstructed inside this museum, and the lifestyle and culture of that time period are nostalgically revived. At the entrance, there is a penny candy store selling everyone’s favorites from time gone by. Continuing on, there is a barbershop, a photo studio, and a general store. Many nostalgic items are on display, and visitors can see and feel the good old days.

events.name: Relax at Hotel
events.desc: After a long day, kick back and relax!

events.name: Takayama Festival Floats Hall
events.desc: This Float Hall is in Sakurayamahachiman, and houses 11 floats for the fall Takayama festival. The floats are rotated three times a year (March, July, and November), putting four on display each time. In a revival of the festival parade, a shrine maiden takes visitors on a tour.

events.name: Matsuri no Mori Museum
events.desc: From the museum's entrance, an approximately 50-meter long hallway leads to the main exhibition space which is located underground, giving it a cave-like atmosphere. The hallway is lined on the left by eleven miniature festival floats, one third the size of those used in the autumn festival. On the right are ostentatious golden-lacquered folding screens which depict famous floats from festivals in Kyoto and other cities.

events.name: Scenic Bus Ride
events.desc: Travel through the mountains to Shirakawa-go.

events.name: Purin-no-Ie
events.desc:
Opened in November 2021 by local artisans, Purin-no-Ie handcrafts its signature “Mizu Purin”—a layered dessert made with the area’s pristine spring water, a creamy custard, and caramel sauce—which earned the inaugural Grand Prix at the Japan Purin Awards in 2022. The shop uses only the finest locally sourced ingredients and fills its puddings in reusable glass jars, making each delicious spoonful a taste of Shirakawa‑go’s natural beauty and artisanal spirit.

 Autumn Seasonal Puddings: Sweet Potato, Persimmon, Kiwi.

events.name: Ogimachi Castle Observation Deck
events.desc: The Ogimachi Castle Site Scenic Lookout affords visitors unimpeded views over the village of Ogimachi, the central settlement in Shirakawa-go and part of the “Historic Villages of Shirakawa-go and Gokayama” World Heritage Site. The landscape that spreads out beneath the hilltop lookout is dotted with gassho-style houses characterized by their steeply slanted, triangular roofs, and makes for an impressive sight throughout the year.

events.name: Travel to Kyoto
events.desc:
• Walk to Takayama Station 
 • Hida Limited Express Train to Kyoto Station 
 • Walk to Machiya

events.name: Drop Stuff Off at Machiya Townhouse
events.desc: Stop for a brief moment to drop stuff off and get ready to go exploring.

events.name: Kiyomizu-dera
events.desc: Kiyomizu-dera, meaning “Pure Water Temple,” is a renowned Buddhist temple in Kyoto, famous for its wooden stage and waterfall. It's a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a popular tourist destination known for its stunning views and spiritual significance.

events.name: Gion
events.desc: Gion is Kyoto's most famous and well-preserved entertainment district, renowned for its geisha culture, traditional wooden machiya townhouses, and narrow, atmospheric streets. It's a popular destination for tourists seeking to experience traditional Japanese culture and see geiko (Kyoto dialect for geisha) and maiko (geiko apprentices).

events.name: Nishiki Market
events.desc: Nishiki Market, also known as “Kyoto's Kitchen,” is a vibrant, five-block-long covered market in central Kyoto. It's a historic area with over 130 shops and restaurants, offering a wide array of fresh produce, seafood, traditional Kyoto specialties, and unique local foods.

events.name: Kichikichi Omurice
events.desc: Kichi Kichi Omurice, a popular Japanese restaurant in Kyoto, is known for its theatrical and delicious omurice (omelette rice) performance. The dish features a fluffy, runny omelet artfully placed and sliced over a bed of flavorful fried rice, often with a theatrical flair by the chef. The restaurant uses a demi-glace sauce instead of ketchup, offering a more elegant and savory taste.

events.name: Ramen Sen-no-Kaze Kyoto
events.desc: From the thousand-year history of Kyoto to the thousand winds in the sky, Ramen Sen-no-Kaze presents an unforgettable taste carefully prepared for each and every one of their customers. In line with their store's concept of health-friendly ramen, they present quality ingredients and a delicious taste in every bowl. Their ingredients are natural and safe, and the tonkotsu (pork-based) soup comes in three delicious varieties: the slightly salty Shio, the soy sauce-based Shoyu, and the popular Miso ramen. Also on offer are ramen dishes such as seafood-based Sen no Shio, seafood/soy sauce-based Kii Soba, and a delightfully simple Su Ramen.

events.name: Kodai-ji
events.desc: Kodai-ji is a prominent Zen Buddhist temple in Kyoto, known for its historical significance and beautiful gardens. Founded in 1606 by samurai Toyotomi Hideyoshi's wife, Kita-no-Mandokoro (also known as Nene), in memory of her late husband, it stands as a testament to their love and Hideyoshi's legacy. The temple complex features a variety of attractions, including a rock garden, bamboo grove, and two historic teahouses designed by the legendary tea master Sen no Rikyu.

events.name: Shinshō Gokurakuji (Shinnyodō) Temple
events.desc: Shinshō Gokurakuji (Shinnyodō) Temple, a hidden gem in Kyoto, is a Buddhist temple of the Tendai sect known for its peaceful atmosphere and beautiful scenery, especially during autumn and spring. Established in 984, it features a main hall with an enshrined Amida Buddha, designated as an important cultural property. The temple grounds include dry landscape gardens, a three-story pagoda, and various buildings, with free entry to most areas and a small fee for the inner chamber of the main hall and gardens.

events.name: Eikando Temple
events.desc: Eikando Temple, also known as Zenrin-ji, is a renowned Buddhist temple in Kyoto, famous for its stunning autumn foliage and a unique Amida Buddha statue. It's the head temple of the Seizan branch of the Jodo-shu (Pure Land) Buddhist sect. The temple is known for its expansive grounds, covered walkways connecting various buildings, and a pond garden that is particularly beautiful during the autumn season.

events.name: Tsukigase Plum Grove
events.desc: Tsukigase Plum Grove in Nara, is a renowned plum blossom viewing spot, featuring a stunning landscape of over 10,000 plum trees that bloom in shades of red, pink, and white, according to local tourism websites. The grove, stretching along the Nabari River, is known for its scenic beauty and is one of Nara's three major plum viewing locations. Visitors can enjoy the fragrant blossoms, picturesque views, and participate in events like the Tsukigase Plum Festival, which features traditional performances and local delicacies.

events.name: Todai-ji
events.desc: Todai-ji is a large Buddhist temple complex in Nara, renowned for its giant bronze Buddha statue and the largest wooden building in the world that houses it. It was a center of Buddhist power and learning during the Nara period.

events.name: Isui-en Garden and Neiraku Museum
events.desc: Isui-en is a Japanese garden located in Nara, the old capital of Japan near Kyōto. It has been preserved since its creation in the Meiji era, and is the only walking garden in Nara. It is divided into two sections, which were originally two separate gardens, and each features a pagoda.

events.name: Wakakusayama Hill
events.desc: Wakakusayama Hill, also known as Mount Wakakusa, is a 342-meter-high hill in Nara, famous for its scenic views and the annual Wakakusa Yamayaki festival. It's a popular spot for hiking and offers panoramic views of Nara city and its surrounding landscape.

events.name: Nara Park
events.desc: Nara Park, established in 1880, is a sprawling public park in Nara, known for its free-roaming Sika deer and historical attractions. It's a popular destination for both locals and tourists, offering a unique blend of natural beauty and cultural significance.

events.name: Manyo Botanical Gardens
events.desc: Manyo Botanical Garden, situated within the precincts of Kasuga Taisha Shrine, has 300 kinds of plants, all mentioned in Manyo-shu (Ten-Thousand Tanka: the oldest anthology of tanka poems). The over 200 wisteria swaying in the wind symbolizes the Fujiwara clan, who originally enshrined their guardian god here at the foot of Kasuga Hill. There is a Japanese teahouse ‘Ninai-jaya’ on the long approach to the shrine. The entrance of the garden is just behind the teahouse.

events.name: Naramachi Karakuri Toy Museum
events.desc: Naramachi Karakuri Toy Museum is a traditional machiya (townhouse) in Naramachi, and is an experience-based facility where you can touch and play with old-fashioned toys.  It was established by Nara City as a place for intergenerational exchanges where children and the elderly can play together, and as a place for local people and tourists to deepen connections.

events.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
events.desc: Fushimi Inari Taisha is a prominent Shinto shrine in Kyoto, famous for its thousands of vermilion torii gates that wind up the mountain behind its main buildings. Dedicated to Inari, the god of rice, prosperity, and business, it is the head shrine for all Inari shrines in Japan. The shrine's trails lead up Mount Inari, encompassing a complex of smaller shrines and offering a unique journey through the natural landscape.

events.name: Tofuku-ji
events.desc: Tofuku-ji is a large, historic Zen Buddhist temple complex in Kyoto, renowned for its stunning autumn foliage and expansive grounds. Founded in 1236, it's one of the Five Great Zen Temples of Kyoto and the head temple of the Tofuku-ji school of the Rinzai sect. The temple is famous for its numerous sub-temples, Zen gardens, and the Tsutenkyo Bridge, which offers spectacular views of maple trees during the fall.

events.name: Nintendo Museum
events.desc: Opened in October 2024, the Nintendo Museum, located in Uji, Kyoto, offers a deep dive into Nintendo's history, showcasing its evolution from playing card manufacturer to global gaming giant. It features interactive exhibits, displays of classic consoles and games, and even workshops where visitors can create their own Hanafuda cards. The museum also includes a boutique with exclusive merchandise and a café with Nintendo-themed decor.

events.name: Kyoto Aquarium
events.desc: Kyoto Aquarium, opened in 2012, is Japan's first aquarium to exclusively use man-made seawater. It's the largest inland aquarium in Japan, housing around 250 species and 15,000 specimens. The aquarium focuses on showcasing aquatic life found in and around Kyoto, with exhibits themed around the region's rivers and sea life. It's known for its interactive “edutainment” approach, combining education and entertainment, and features popular attractions like dolphin shows, penguins, seals, and a unique zone dedicated to the Japanese giant salamander.

events.name: Hozugawa Kudari
events.desc: Hozugawa Kudari, also known as the Hozugawa River Boat Ride, is a scenic boat tour in Kyoto. It offers a 16-kilometer, two-hour journey down the Hozu River, from Kameoka to Arashiyama. The ride is known for its beautiful scenery, including lush greenery, dramatic cliffs, and unique rock formations, as well as sections of calm waters and thrilling rapids.

events.name: Arashiyama Monkey Park
events.desc: Iwatayama Monkey Park is a commercial park located in Arashiyama in Kyoto. The park is located atop Mount Arashiyama, on the opposite side of the Ōi River of the train station. It is inhabited by a troop of over 120 Japanese macaque monkeys.

events.name: Arashiyama Yusai-Tei Gallery
events.desc: The Arashiyama Yusai-tei Gallery, also known as Somekobo Yume Yusai, is a 150-year-old building in Kyoto's Arashiyama district, known for its dyeing art and unique architecture. It features a gallery showcasing the owner's Yume Kouro Dyeing technique, as well as installations like reflective tables and “water mirrors” that reflect the surrounding nature. The gallery also offers a serene environment with a tea room and opportunities to participate in dyeing workshops.

events.name: Kinkaku-ji
events.desc: Kinkaku-ji, also known as the Golden Pavilion, is a stunning Zen Buddhist temple in Kyoto, famous for its shimmering gold leaf exterior. Originally built as a retirement villa for a shogun, it was converted into a temple after his death. The three-story structure is renowned for its unique architectural style, blending elements of Heian-period palaces, samurai residences, and Zen temples. The pavilion's reflection in the surrounding pond, Kyoko-chi, adds to its breathtaking beauty.

events.name: Nijo Castle
events.desc: Nijo Castle, a flatland castle in Kyoto, served as the Kyoto residence for the Tokugawa shoguns. It's a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its impressive architecture, including the Ninomaru Palace, and beautiful gardens. The castle is divided into three main areas: Honmaru, Ninomaru, and gardens. The Ninomaru Palace is particularly famous for its “nightingale floors” which squeak when walked on, designed to alert guards to intruders.

events.name: Kyoto International Manga Museum
events.desc: The Kyoto International Manga Museum is a unique cultural facility that combines the functions of a manga museum and a library. It houses a vast collection of over 300,000 manga and manga-related materials, including both historical and contemporary works from Japan and abroad. The museum also features special exhibitions, research programs, and events related to manga culture. Visitors can browse through a large portion of the collection, with many books available to read on-site, making it feel more like a library than a museum.

events.name: BONCHI Kyoto Miniature
events.desc: BONCHI Kyoto Miniature is a workshop in Kyoto, where you can learn to make detailed miniature food samples using polymer clay and other materials. It's run by a friendly couple who are passionate about handcrafted miniatures. The workshop offers a variety of miniature food options, from desserts like strawberry tarts to savory dishes like fried rice or noodles.

events.name: Travel to Osaka
events.desc:
• Walk to Kyoto Station 
 • Kintetsu Limited Express to Yamato-Saidaiji Station 
 • Kintetsu-Nara Line Rapid Express to Osaka-Namba Station 
 • Walk to Hotel

events.name: Drop Stuff Off at Hotel
events.desc: Henn na Hotel, meaning “Strange Hotel” in Japanese, is a unique hotel chain known for its use of advanced technology and robots, particularly at the front desk for check-in and throughout the hotel for various services. The hotel aims to provide a futuristic and convenient experience for guests, while also evolving to meet changing needs.

events.name: Osaka Museum of Natural History
events.desc: The Osaka Museum of Natural History, established in 1974, explores the relationship between humanity and nature. It's located in Nagai Park and features over a million specimens including fossils, plants, and animals. The museum focuses on themes like the natural world, the history of earth and life, evolution, and the lives of living things. Notable exhibits include reconstructed skeletons of prehistoric creatures and interactive displays.

events.name: teamLab Botanical Garden
events.desc: teamLab Botanical Garden in Osaka is a unique, interactive art space within Nagai Botanical Garden, transforming the natural environment into a mesmerizing nighttime experience. By day, it's a serene botanical garden; after dark, it comes alive with digital art installations that respond to the environment and visitor interactions. The artworks, including glowing ovoids, sculptures responding to wind and birds, and illuminated pathways, blend seamlessly with the natural elements, blurring the lines between art and nature.

events.name: Spa World
events.desc: Spa World is a destination offering a variety of spa and wellness experiences, often inspired by international bathing and sauna traditions. It features facilities like onsen (hot springs), stone saunas, swimming pools, and beauty treatments, with a focus on relaxation and rejuvenation. Some locations also incorporate elements like Korean-style jjimjilbangs (sauna), beauty salons, and dining options.

events.name: Umeda Sky Building
events.desc: The Umeda Sky Building is a unique architectural landmark in Osaka, known for its two 40-story towers connected by a floating garden observatory. This distinctive design, completed in 1993, has made it a popular tourist attraction and a symbol of the city. Visitors can enjoy panoramic views of Osaka from the observatory, located 173 meters above ground.

events.name: Osaka Municipal Housing Museum
events.desc: The Osaka Museum of Housing and Living, also known as the Osaka Municipal Housing Museum, offers a unique and immersive experience of Osaka's history and culture, focusing on the evolution of housing and lifestyles from the Edo period to the Showa period. Visitors can explore reconstructed streets and buildings, including a detailed recreation of an Edo-era townscape with shops, houses, and even a river. The museum also features exhibits on the Meiji, Taisho, and Showa eras, showcasing how housing and living conditions changed over time.

events.name: Osaka Castle
events.desc: Osaka Castle is a magnificent landmark in Osaka, renowned for its historical significance and stunning architecture. Originally built in the late 16th century by samurai Toyotomi Hideyoshi, it served as a military stronghold and a symbol of his power during the unification of Japan. The castle, rebuilt multiple times throughout history, is now a five-story donjon (keep) surrounded by moats and stone walls. It houses a museum dedicated to the castle's history and Toyotomi Hideyoshi, offering panoramic city views from its top floor.

events.name: National Museum of Ethnology
events.desc: The National Museum of Ethnology (Minpaku) in Osaka, is a world-renowned institution dedicated to the study and display of cultural anthropology and ethnology. It houses a vast collection of artifacts, objects, and media representing diverse cultures globally, with a focus on daily life, rituals, and performing arts. The museum also functions as a research institute and graduate school, contributing to a deeper understanding of human societies and cultures.

events.name: Nakanoshima Museum of Art
events.desc: The Nakanoshima Museum of Art, Osaka (NAKKA) is a contemporary art museum located in the Nakanoshima district of Osaka. It opened on February 2, 2022. The museum features a distinctive black, cube-like exterior and a public “passage” designed to make art accessible to everyone. Its collection boasts over 6,000 works of modern and contemporary art and design, including pieces by both international and Japanese artists, with a focus on art from the mid-19th century to the present.

events.name: Cup Noodles Museum Osaka Ikeda
events.desc: CupNoodles Museum Osaka Ikeda is a museum dedicated to instant noodles and Cup Noodles, as well as its creator and founder, Momofuku Ando. The museum is located in Ikeda in Osaka, and is within walking distance of Ikeda Station on the Hankyu-Takarazuka Line.

events.name: Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan
events.desc: Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan is one of the world's largest aquariums, known for its innovative exhibits and diverse marine life. It recreates the natural environments of the Pacific Rim, featuring 14 large tanks including the central “Pacific Ocean” tank, which is 9 meters deep and houses whale sharks. The aquarium showcases over 30,000 marine animals representing 620 species, allowing visitors to experience the wonders of the Pacific Ocean up close.

events.name: Unimocc Art Café
events.desc: Unimocc Art Café is a unique Japanese café in Osaka where customers can decorate their own cake, blending art and culinary experiences. Customers can order a plain white cake and a variety of art supplies to create a personalized masterpiece. The cafe also offers art-inspired drinks like the “Impression, Sunrise” vanilla almond latte.

events.name: Denden Town
events.desc: Denden Town, also known as Nipponbashi, is a vibrant shopping district in Osaka, famous for its electronics, anime, manga, and otaku culture. Often called the “Akihabara of the West” (referring to Tokyo's similar district), it offers a wide array of specialty stores, arcades, maid cafés, and more.

events.name: Shinsekai
events.desc: Shinsekai, meaning “New World,” is a vibrant, retro-style district in Osaka. Developed in the early 20th century, it was initially designed with Parisian and New York (Coney Island) influences, symbolized by Tsutenkaku Tower. Today, it's known for its bustling nightlife, affordable eateries, and nostalgic atmosphere, offering a glimpse into Osaka's past.

events.name: Dotonbori
events.desc: Dotonbori is a vibrant, bustling entertainment district in Osaka, known for its bright neon lights, lively atmosphere, and delicious local cuisine. It's a popular spot for tourists and locals alike, offering a wide range of attractions, including restaurants, bars, clubs, and shops. The area is centered around the Dotonbori Canal, and features iconic landmarks like the Glico Running Man sign and the Kani Doraku crab restaurant.

events.name: Osaka Ukiyo-e Museum
events.desc: The Osaka Ukiyo-e Museum, located in the Shinsaibashi shopping district, is dedicated to the art of Ukiyo-e woodblock prints. It features works by renowned artists like Katsushika Hokusai, Utagawa Hiroshige, and others, with a focus on prints related to Osaka and Kyoto. The museum also has a shop selling Ukiyo-e related books, goods, and replica prints.

events.name: Moonshine Karaoke Bar
events.desc: Moonshine Karaoke Bar is a lively venue in Osaka, known for its fun and inclusive atmosphere where both locals and tourists can enjoy singing karaoke. It's a place where people from diverse backgrounds come together to share music and stories. The bar offers a wide selection of songs in multiple languages, including English and Japanese, and provides a space for both individual performances and group fun.

events.name: A Happy Pancake
events.desc: A Happy Pancake, also known as Shiawase no Pancake (幸せのパンケーキ), is a Japanese pancake restaurant known for its incredibly fluffy and soft soufflé-style pancakes. These pancakes are made with a batter incorporating whipped egg whites, giving them a light, airy, and almost pudding-like texture. They are often served with toppings like Manuka honey whipped butter, caramel syrup, or seasonal fruits.

events.name: Okonomiyaki Okaru
events.desc: Okonomiyaki Okaru is a well-regarded okonomiyaki restaurant in Osaka, known for its traditional Osaka-style okonomiyaki, a savory pancake dish. The restaurant, established in 1946, offers a retro atmosphere and a hands-on experience where staff prepare the okonomiyaki on a hot griddle in front of the customers. A popular feature is the mayonnaise art they create on top of the dish, often depicting local landmarks or cartoon characters.

events.name: Universal Studios Japan
events.desc: Universal Studios Japan, located in Osaka, is a popular theme park featuring immersive areas based on movies, games, and popular characters. It's known for its thrilling rides, shows, and seasonal events, offering a diverse range of entertainment for all ages. Key attractions include Super Nintendo World, The Wizarding World of Harry Potter, and Minion Park, alongside areas like Jurassic Park and Universal Wonderland. The park's most recent addition, Donkey Kong Country, opened in December 2024.

events.desc:
• Walk to Osaka-Namba Station 
 • Midosuji Line to Shin-Osaka Station  
 • Tokaido Shinkansen to Odawara Station 
 • Hakone Tozan Line to Hakone-Yumoto Station 
 • Bus to Deyama Bus Stop 
 • Walk to Ryokan

events.name: Hakone Shrine
events.desc: Hakone Shrine, a Shinto shrine nestled on the shores of Lake Ashi in Hakone, is a place of spiritual significance and natural beauty. It's known for its iconic red torii gate that appears to float on the lake, ancient cedar trees, and historical connection to warriors and travelers.

events.name: Relax at Ryokan
events.desc: As the evening rolls in, most things will be closed by this point, so enjoy the volcanic mountainside, ryokan atmosphere, and private onsen!

events.name: Ōwakudani
events.desc: Ōwakudani is a volcanic valley with active sulphur vents and hot springs in Hakone, Kanagawa Prefecture. It was created around 3,000 years ago, as a result of the eruption of the Hakone volcano.

events.name: Hakone Geo Museum
events.desc: The Hakone Geo Museum, located in Owakudani, focuses on the geological wonders of the Hakone region, particularly its volcanic activity. It offers exhibits about the area's volcanoes, hot springs, and unique geological formations. Visitors can learn about the history of the area's terrain, including Ōwakudani, Lake Ashi, Sengokuhara, and Hakone Onsen, all shaped by volcanic activity. The museum also provides information on volcanic gas and disaster prevention in Ōwakudani.

events.name: Hakone Open-Air Museum
events.desc: The Hakone Open-Air Museum, is an outdoor sculpture gallery that plays with nature. Situated in the mountains of Hakone, it spreads across 70,000 square meters and has beautiful views of the surrounding mountains. This art museum opened in 1969 and was the very first outdoor gallery in Japan.

events.name: Hakone Venetian Glass Museum
events.desc: The Hakone Venetian Glass Museum, also known as Hakone Glass no Mori, is Japan's first museum dedicated to Venetian glass, showcasing exquisite pieces from the 15th to 19th centuries and modern works. Located in the lush greenery of Hakone's Sengokuhara, the museum features a beautiful garden inspired by medieval Venice, complete with ponds, sculptures, and spots for photos. Visitors can enjoy the delicate beauty of Venetian glass, appreciate the craftsmanship, and relax at the café-restaurant while enjoying live Italian song performances.

events.name: Yunessun
events.desc: Yunessun is a hot springs theme park in Hakone, known for its unique and playful approach to onsen (hot spring) experiences. It features two main areas: Yunessun, where visitors can enjoy various themed baths in swimwear, and Mori no Yu, a traditional Japanese onsen area. Yunessun offers attractions like the “Rodeo Mountain” water slide and baths filled with wine, coffee, and other unique concoctions. Mori no Yu provides a more serene experience with open-air baths and views of the Hakone mountains.

events.name: Hakone Forest Adventure
events.desc: Hakone Forest Adventure is an outdoor park in Hakone, offering a variety of treetop adventure courses for all ages. It's known for its zip lines, obstacle courses, and tree climbing activities, all set within a beautiful natural landscape. The park features both an “Adventure Course” for a more challenging experience and a “Canopy Course” suitable for families and children.

events.name: Sengokuhara Grass Fields
events.desc: The Sengokuhara Grass Fields, also known as the Sengokuhara Susuki Grass Fields, are a vast area in Hakone, renowned for its stunning pampas grass (susuki) that turns a shimmering golden color in autumn. Located on the slopes of Mt. Daigatake, the fields offer scenic views, especially from late September to early November. A walking trail allows visitors to immerse themselves in the beauty of the swaying grass and surrounding mountains.

events.name: Hakone Gora Park
events.desc: Hakone Gora Park is a French-style landscape garden. It's known for its beautiful seasonal flowers, a large fountain, a rose garden, and two greenhouses. The park also offers craft activities like glass blowing and pottery, and a traditional Japanese tea house.

events.name: POLA Museum of Art
events.desc: The POLA Museum of Art, located in Hakone, is known for its striking architecture and its collection of Western and Japanese art, with a particular emphasis on Impressionist and École de Paris works. The museum is designed to blend with its natural surroundings, with the majority of the building underground, and features large windows that offer views of the surrounding forest. The museum also has a nature trail for visitors to explore the surrounding scenery.

events.name: Drop Stuff Off at Hotel
events.desc: Drop our stuff off and get ready to go for the day!

events.name: teamLab Borderless
events.desc: teamLab Borderless is a digital art museum in Tokyo where visitors wander through a borderless world of interconnected, interactive installations. It's a place where art flows from one space to another, creating a continuous, immersive experience. The museum, created by the art collective teamLab, encourages exploration, discovery, and interaction with the art and other visitors.

events.name: Azabudai Hills Mori JP Garden Terrace
events.desc: The Azabudai Hills Mori JP Garden Terrace is a prominent feature of the Azabudai Hills complex in Tokyo. It embodies the “Modern Urban Village” concept, which focuses on creating a large, open space filled with greenery to foster community and well-being.

events.name: Shibuya Crossing
events.desc: Shibuya Crossing, also known as Shibuya Scramble Crossing, is a famous pedestrian intersection located in front of Shibuya Station in Tokyo. It's renowned for its massive crowds of people crossing from all directions when the traffic lights turn red, earning it the nickname “scramble”.

events.name: Shibuya Parco
events.desc: Shibuya Parco is a prominent commercial complex in Tokyo's Shibuya district, known for its diverse offerings across fashion, art, entertainment, dining, and technology. It's a multi-story building featuring a mix of shops, galleries, restaurants, and entertainment venues, including the first official Nintendo store in Japan and the Pokemon Center Shibuya.

events.name: RuRu Café
events.desc: RURU SHIBUYA is a café in Shibuya, Tokyo, known for its unique “water table” concept and serene Japanese garden atmosphere. Drinks and desserts are served on clear platters that appear to float on the water, creating a calming, zen-like experience. The café is located on the 2nd floor of the Shibuya Sakura Stage, offering a tranquil escape in the heart of the bustling city.

events.name: Miyashita Park
events.desc: Miyashita Park is a multi-level complex in Shibuya, Tokyo, that combines shopping, dining, sports facilities, and a rooftop park. It's a popular destination for both locals and tourists, offering a variety of activities and experiences.

events.name: Shibuya Stream
events.desc: Shibuya Stream is a modern complex in Tokyo's Shibuya district, featuring a skyscraper with offices and a hotel, along with retail and dining spaces. It's known for its blend of urban renewal, connecting to the revitalized Shibuya River and offering a mix of casual and gourmet dining options.

events.name: Shibuya 109
events.desc: Shibuya 109 is a prominent shopping mall in Tokyo's Shibuya district, known for its focus on trendy fashion and cosmetics for young women and teenagers. It features over 120 shops spread across 10 floors, offering a wide variety of items like clothing, accessories, and beauty products.

events.name: Hikarie
events.desc: Shibuya Hikarie is a modern skyscraper in the Shibuya district of Tokyo, known for its blend of shopping, dining, and cultural experiences. It houses the ShinQs shopping area with fashion, beauty, and food, alongside theaters, event spaces, and offices.

events.name: Shibuya Sakura Stage
events.desc: Shibuya Sakura Stage is a large-scale complex located in the Sakuragaoka area of Shibuya, Tokyo, designed to be a new gateway to the vibrant district. It combines work, play, and residence, featuring cutting-edge digital spaces, lush greenery, plazas, and terraces.

events.name: teamLab Planets
events.desc: teamLab Planets in Tokyo is a body-immersive museum where visitors experience art through their senses, often while barefoot and sometimes submerged in water. The museum features large-scale, interactive artworks that blend reality and fantasy using light, sound, water, and mirrors. It's located in Toyosu and is known for its unique, sensory-rich environment.

events.name: Tokyo Joypolis
events.desc: Tokyo Joypolis is an indoor theme park located in Odaiba, Tokyo, offering a range of attractions including rides, arcade games, and virtual reality experiences. It's known for its diverse offerings, from thrill rides like the Gekion Live Coaster and Halfpipe Tokyo to interactive games and classic arcade favorites. The park is spread across three floors of the DECKS Tokyo Beach shopping complex.

events.name: Gundam Base Tokyo
events.desc: The Gundam Base Tokyo is a comprehensive Gunpla (Gundam plastic model) facility located in DiverCity Tokyo Plaza in Odaiba. It's designed as an official space for Gundam fans of all levels, offering a space to buy, build, see, and learn about Gunpla. The facility features multiple zones, including a shop with a vast selection of kits, a builders' area, a factory zone showcasing the manufacturing process, and an event zone for special displays and limited-edition items.

events.name: Miraikan
events.desc: Miraikan, officially the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation, is a science museum in Tokyo, Japan, dedicated to showcasing cutting-edge science and technology. It aims to connect people with the latest advancements in fields like space exploration, robotics, and the global environment, encouraging discussions about the future. Miraikan features interactive exhibits, workshops, and talks, making it a popular destination for both adults and children.

events.name: Tokyo Trick Art Museum
events.desc: Located on the fourth floor of Decks Tokyo Beach in Odaiba, this museum offers immersive 2D paintings that cleverly trick the eye into seeming three-dimensional—especially themed around vivid Edo-period scenes. Visitors are encouraged to become the “director” of their own photos as they interact with dramatic ninja, spirits, and historical artworks.

events.name: Unko Museum Tokyo
events.desc: The Unko Museum is a unique, poop-themed entertainment facility where visitors can experience the “max unko kawaii” (disgustingly cute) world of poop through various interactive exhibits and photo opportunities. It aims to change perceptions about poop and offer a fun, playful environment for all ages
